notes.2ii: This part was well answered, though occasionally candidates failed to substitute their values of a and b to obtain a linear expression. Only rarely was gf used instead of fg.
notes.3i: Most candidates used the scalar product accurately and set this to 0, though −1 and 90 were common errors. Unfortunately many candidates produced a mass of working through not appreciating that =0 implies that a = 0.
notes.4ii: Several candidates failed to realise the need to obtain a quadratic equation in x or in y and then to set “b2 – 4ac” to 0. Algebraic errors in the coefficients of a, b and c were common, particularly with those candidates taking the longer route of obtaining a quadratic equation in x. A small minority attempted the alternative method of equating gradients, but these were rarely correct.
notes.5i: Despite many curves being too straight or y = cos2x being parabolic, most candidates obtained some marks for this part and most obtained the correct end-points for both curves. Many candidates unnecessarily drew accurate graphs and wasted a considerable amount of time.
notes.5ii: Stating that x = 30° because it looks approximately correct on a sketch graph gained no credit. Candidates should realise that “verify” implies showing that sin30° and cos60° have the same value. Very few candidates realised that the other root (by symmetry or otherwise) was 150°.
notes.6i: Many candidate lost a mark through not explaining why the height was 3 3. In a question requesting “show”, it is insufficient to state that 6sin60 = 3 3.
notes.6ii: Although a few candidates mistakenly used “arc length” for “ sector area”, the majority used the formula s = rθ correctly to find the arcs DX and EX. Finding the length of DE proved difficult with the majority failing to realise that DE = 16 − 6cos60 − 10cosθ. The final accuracy mark was also often lost through not stating the answer to the accuracy requested.
notes.7i: Whilst the majority of candidates realised the need to find the gradient of the line and to equate the product of this and to −1, there were many errors. notes.general_comments: General comments The paper allowed the majority of candidates to show what they had learned and understood. It was particularly the case in this paper that quite a number of questions contained a straightforward part, or parts, followed by a part that was more searching. This allowed even weaker candidates to score a reasonable number of marks and also gave stronger candidates the opportunity to demonstrate their understanding and ability on the more demanding parts of questions.
